result.proposed_fix: (R1-03) Measure ink with the page's decorations out of the way. In probe.js add a global 'nodeco' rule to the adopted sheet ('*,*::before,*::after{text-decoration-line:none !important;text-emphasis:none !important}') and turn it on for the clear, tint and tint2 shots. Add one extra 'base_nodeco' screenshot (real page, decorations off). In onscreen._counts count a pixel as inked only when base_nodeco differs from clear by OWN_DELTA and base equals base_nodeco within OWN_DELTA, so the glyph shows without decorations and no decoration paints over it. In onscreen.load require the new shot and drop all page text when it is missing. Optionally have probe.js report each unit's computed fill colour and require inked base pixels to be near it. Add a self-contained Chromium regression test with the white-text/black-line-through and #dcdcdc variants embedded. (R1-01) Canonicalise once, in untrusted.normalise, and use the result for both the check and the display: NFKC, then delete every Unicode Cf character (U+200B-U+200F, U+2060, U+00AD, U+FEFF, ...), then map U+3002, U+FF0E and U+FF61 to '.'. Allow Unicode letters and digits in labels ([^\W_]), and accept a TLD in any case and script when it is followed by '/' or the label before it has a hyphen or digit, or when it is in a known-TLD list. Keep 'rose.The' as not a link by requiring a lowercase TLD or one of those signals. Have surface.clean and uri_a2ui/validate._URLISH use untrusted.normalise plus LINK_PATTERN (the validator refuses any match). Test with all six round-2 strings, plus one ResearchJob(use_brain=False) case end to end. (R1-02) Make D7 independent of the word list: show a claim unquoted only when its normalised tokens are a contiguous run of the supporting source sentence's tokens (function words may be dropped only at the ends); otherwise quote_instead(). Keep states_quantity as a second check. Test with the order-of-magnitude, hourly, fortnight and nineties cases.
result.root_cause: Three defects, one pattern: each control is a list of known-bad forms, and each repair added only the reviewer's example strings. (R1-03) probe.js removes and recolours the text with a CSS ::highlight. Chromium cannot remove the originating element's text-decoration through a highlight; it repaints that decoration in the highlight colour, so 'text-decoration:none !important' in the highlight rule (probe.js:68-69) does nothing. A line-through bar is therefore transparent in the 'clear' shot and takes both tints like real glyph pixels. onscreen.Probe._counts (onscreen.py:176-213) counts a pixel as the unit's own ink when base differs from clear and tint/tint2 match the palettes. The black bar over white text passes every test, so the hidden text reaches the Brain as 'pixel-checked'. The check never asks whether the base pixel is the glyph's own colour or whether the glyph is visible without its decorations. (R1-01) untrusted.LINK_PATTERN (untrusted.py:44-47) is an ASCII-only regex: labels are [A-Za-z0-9-], the TLD must be all lower or all upper case, and the only canonicalisation is NFKC (untrusted.py:51), which keeps U+200B, U+00AD and U+3002 and leaves Cyrillic letters as they are. surface.clean strips only characters below U+0020, so zero-width and soft-hyphen characters stay in the rendered text. The A2UI last-line check validate._URLISH (validate.py:19) is still the old '\b' scheme-only regex. (R1-02) Whether D7 is enforced still depends on states_quantity, a word list (synthesize.py:74-84, 99). The fallback _in_order (synthesize.py:125-130) is a subsequence test: it uses one shared iterator, so words may be skipped between matches. A claim that joins the subject of one clause to the quantity of another passes with no new word and in order, and is shown unquoted.
result.why_earlier_repairs_failed: ca622bc lists R1-03 in its message but changes neither onscreen.py nor probe.js. Its assist-side changes (redact.py, snapshot.js, perception.py, tests/assist/test_a0_r16_url_secret_regressions.py) are all for R1-04, the URL secrets, so R1-03 got no code and no test. For R1-01 it widened the regex to the reviewer's five strings (the LINKS tuple in tests/web/test_w1_r16_review_regressions.py) and added NFKC, but it did not remove format characters, map ideographic dots, allow non-ASCII labels or accept mixed-case TLDs. It also left uri_a2ui/validate._URLISH unchanged, although the finding named it. For R1-02 it added the reviewer's quantity words (tenfold, percentage, decade, couple, Phase V) and an _in_order check that tests a subsequence, not a contiguous run, so D7 still rests on the word list. The tests check exactly the reviewer's examples, so they pass while each new variant fails.

result.proposed_fix: Make both checks fail closed and keep the lists as an extra check only. (A) untrusted._is_domain: any ASCII 'label<dot>tld' with a 2+ letter alphabetic TLD is a link, in any case. Remove the case/_TLDS/hyphen heuristics. A missing space after a full stop ('rose.The') then counts as a link: verify/extractive drop or skip that sentence and the surface masks it. That only costs precision, never safety. Rewrite the precision tests at test_w1_r2_review_regressions.py:43-48 and test_w1_r16_review_regressions.py:47 so that 'rose.The', 'so.Then' and 'rose.Été' are expected to be flagged, keeping the real non-link cases ('e.g.', 'U.S.', '4.5%', 'a.m.', 'Ph.D', CJK '。'). Add spaced defangs to _DOT: \s*\[\s*\.\s*\]\s*, \s*\(\s*\.\s*\)\s*, \s+dot\s+ when followed by an alphabetic TLD. Add a phone/contact pattern (\+?\d[\d\s().-]{6,}\d with ≥8 digits). Because surface.clean masks one whitespace-separated token at a time, it must also mask the spaced forms over the whole matched span, not only within one token. Self-contained regression tests: 'Refundsportal.Cash', 'refundsportal.Lol', 'refundsportal.CaSh', 'Refundsportal.Exchange', 'Refundsportal.Deals', 'refundsportal [.] com', 'refundsportal dot com', '1800 555 0199', each checked through has_link_or_contact, verify, extractive and build_surface+require_valid. (B) synthesize._excerpt: a non-quoted Brain sentence is shown only if its full token sequence, function words included, is a contiguous run of the supporting source sentence's tokens (MAX_GAP_WORDS=0 and no skipped function words). Otherwise quote_instead(). Do not call states_quantity inside gap_ok. Keep _QUANTITY only as the upfront 'always quote' check, and optionally add doubling/halving/-tupl(ed|ing)/multiplied/bi-?weekly/bi-?monthly/semi-?annual/tri-?ennial/‰/pct/ppm. Regression tests: the five R3-02 pairs plus 'about doubling', 'barely rose' and 'rarely waived' must give quoted=True (the source sentence) or be dropped, never quoted=False with the shortened text.
result.root_cause: Both protections fail open: text is let through by default and only blocked when a list recognises it. (1) Links: untrusted._is_domain (uri_web/untrusted.py:98-104) treats an ASCII 'label.Tld' as a link only if the TLD is all-lower or all-upper, is in a hard-coded ~200-entry _TLDS list, is followed by '/', or the host has a hyphen or digit. Every other mixed-case real gTLD ('Refundsportal.Cash', '.Lol', '.CaSh', '.Exchange', '.Deals') counts as 'not a link'. Spaced defangs ('[.]' with spaces, ' dot ') and phone numbers have no pattern at all. surface.clean, verify() and extractive() all call this one detector, so a miss passes all three (W1-AC15/AC12). The default exists so that 'rose.The' and 'so.Then' are not flagged, and tests enforce that, so the detector cannot fail closed without changing those tests. (2) D7: synthesize._excerpt (uri_web/synthesize.py:141-176) lets a claim skip up to MAX_GAP_WORDS=2 content words, plus any number of function words, as long as gap_ok's states_quantity(text) check finds no quantity in the skipped text. So a qualifier ('nearly', 'possibly', 'about', 'barely', 'rarely') can be dropped next to any quantity or meaning word the _QUANTITY/_ORDINAL lists don't know ('doubling', 'halving', 'quintupled', 'biweekly', ...). The shortened claim is then shown unquoted in the Brain's words. D7 still depends on the word list, even though the code comment says it rests on _excerpt.
result.why_earlier_repairs_failed: Each repair turned the reviewer's examples into more list entries and kept the 'allow if unknown' default. ca622bc (R1-01/R1-02): added a bare-domain regex limited to all-lower/all-upper TLDs so that 'rose.The' still passes, and added tenfold/decade/couple to _QUANTITY. It also added _in_order, which allowed unlimited gaps. f370064 (R2-01/R2-02): canonicalised Unicode, which is correct and general, then decided ambiguous title-case TLDs with a finite _TLDS/_IDN_TLDS list and special cases, and kept the precision tests (test_w1_r16_review_regressions.py:47, test_w1_r2_review_regressions.py:43-48) that require 'rose.The', 'so.Then' and 'rose.Été' not to be flagged. For D7 it replaced the unlimited gaps with a 2-content-word gap whose only quantity guard is states_quantity(), the same list the comment says D7 no longer depends on. It also added more list words (hourly, basis points, ...). Neither repair removed the default that lets unrecognised forms through, so the next unlisted form (R3-01: '.Cash', 'dot com', phone numbers; R3-02: 'doubling', 'biweekly', or plain qualifiers) passes again.

result.root_cause: R3-01: the candidate regex _BARE (uri_web/untrusted.py:64, unchanged since f370064) only accepts a top-level label of 2-24 letters ([^\W\d_]{2,24}) and forbids a hyphen or word character after it ((?![\w-])). A punycode/ACE TLD such as 'xn--p1ai' (digits and hyphens) never produces a match, so _is_domain, which repair 3 made fail closed, is never called. _OTHER and _PHONE don't catch it either, so has_link_or_contact, verify(), extractive(), mask_links and build_surface all let it through. R3-02: _excerpt.gap_ok (uri_web/synthesize.py:166-167) still lets the source drop one determiner plus up to MAX_GAP_WORDS=2 words that aren't function words, and match() (synthesize.py:180) lets the claim omit the determiner. Qualifiers and adverbs sit exactly in that slot ('a roughly decennial cycle', 'a near unanimous decision', 'a barely positive profit'), so whether the claim gets quoted still depends on states_quantity recognising the word. This contradicts the docstring's 'fails closed' claim.
result.why_earlier_repairs_failed: Every repair patched the reported strings and the layer the reviewer pointed at, not the permissive structure. R3-01: f370064 introduced _BARE with a letters-only TLD group plus a TLD allow-list in _is_domain. 462be42 rewrote only _is_domain to fail closed (diff touches _is_domain, _DOT, _PHONE, _SENTENCE_WORDS; the _BARE line is byte-identical in both commits), so anything _BARE can't match is still missed. R3-02: f370064 replaced _in_order with a gap rule allowing any 2 skipped content words and kept states_quantity as the guard. 462be42 narrowed that to 'determiner + 2 non-function words' and added more words to _QUANTITY (doubling, ...tupled, biweekly), but kept the noun-phrase-modifier carve-out. Its invented-word tests only cover qualifiers before verbs, never qualifiers inside a noun phrase after a determiner, so the hole was codified, not closed.

report.notes: Verified: both regression files fail on a clean export of ca622bc (web: 61 failed / 6 guard cases pass both ways; assist: 3 failed, reviewer's STRIKE-PAYLOAD and 4 other payloads leak) and pass after the change. Full tests/assist + tests/web: 2782 passed. R2-03: probe.js takes clear/tint/tint2 with all decorations off (NODECO), adds a 'plain' shot (op 'plain') and a per-unit 'd' flag for decorations it cannot switch off (inline/id !important, decorated ::first-line/::first-letter on the unit or a flat-tree ancestor, a page CSS highlight over the unit); onscreen.py requires 'plain' (missing -> no page text), counts ink only where plain differs from clear and base equals plain, and drops units with 'd' or decorations covering more than 25% of the box ('decorated'). ::first-letter/::first-line are not in NODECO (a rule there splits text runs and moves glyphs, which dropped an ordinary link); the 'd' check covers them. Existing test helpers updated for the new shot (shared Playwright driver in test_a0_r13, synthetic probes in test_a0_r13 and test_a0_d10, plus a missing-plain case); no assertion weakened. R2-01: untrusted.normalise = NFKC + delete default-ignorables, used for detection and display; U+3002/U+FF0E/U+FF61 count as dots; Unicode labels; any-case/IDN TLD accepted when known, followed by '/', or the host has a hyphen/digit; a second pass on an accent-stripped, homoglyph-folded skeleton; surface.clean masks link-bearing tokens through untrusted.mask_links; LINK_PATTERN removed (only surface used it). uri_a2ui/validate._URLISH is outside the permitted paths and unchanged; the surface masks before it runs. R2-02: synthesize._excerpt replaces the subsequence test: matched in order, each gap at most 2 content words and no clause word, clause punctuation or quantity; the claim's own joining words must match the source; memoised. A strictly contiguous rule would break two existing tests (test_w1_d7_verbatim_numbers::test_claim_without_quantity_is_still_checked_not_quoted, test_w1_r9::test_r9_02_any_added_content_word...), so short modifier gaps are allowed; making it fully contiguous is an owner decision. Quantity list extended as a second check only. Not verified: the real extension adapter (docs mark the extension channel NOT IMPLEMENTED) and whether page highlights are visible from the isolated world; only the Playwright stand-in was run. Over-detection: missing-space typos where the next word is a real TLD ('Café.Bar') now count as links (extra masking/quoting only). tests/phase2a/test_frozen_core.py::test_base_commit... fails on the HEAD commit check, unrelated. graphify not run; nothing committed.

R3-01: untrusted._is_domain now blocks by default: any label<dot>label with a 2+ letter last label is a link in any case; the _TLDS/case/hyphen rules no longer decide. Two exceptions remain: a missing space before one of a few non-domain words (_SENTENCE_WORDS: the/then/this/that/these/those/they/été/ete), and the ideographic full stop between two Chinese/Japanese runs unless the second run is in _IDN_TLDS (still list-based; disclosed). Added spaced defangs ([.], ( . ), [dot], (dot), ' dot ', ' . ') to _DOT and a phone pattern (8+ digits, dates and year ranges excluded). mask_links masks the whole matched span across words, look-alike characters included. Existing precision tests left unchanged instead of rewritten as the diagnosis proposed, because rewriting them would weaken existing tests. Not checked: whether the _SENTENCE_WORDS entries are real domain endings (IANA download blocked by the proxy). R3-02: _excerpt matches every claim word in order; the claim may add only determiners; the source may leave out only determiners, or one determiner plus at most MAX_GAP_WORDS words that are not function words (noun-phrase modifiers). Kept because tests d7_verbatim_numbers:40 and r2:140 require 'after a long public consultation' -> 'after consultation' to stay unquoted. states_quantity on the skipped text is kept only as an extra check; added doubling/halving/-tupl(e|ed|ing)/multiplied/bi-weekly/bi-monthly/semi-annual/triennial/quadrennial/‰/ppm/ppb/pct to _QUANTITY. Remaining gap: a modifier inside a determiner-led noun phrase before a noun not recognised as a quantity can still be dropped ('the near zorbing' -> 'the zorbing'). Precision costs: 'red dot appeared', 'US DOT said', 8+ digit runs that are not dates, a missing space before an unlisted word, and claims using a function word the source lacks are now flagged or quoted. Ran the new file against a clean export of f370064: 67 failed, 5 passed (the precision and noun-phrase checks plus 3 quantity forms already detected there). After the change: tests/web + tests/assist 2782 passed. graphify not run (as instructed).

R4-01: _BARE tld group widened from [^\W\d_]{2,24} to (?i:[a-z0-9]{2}--[\w-]{1,59})|[^\W\d_]{2,63}, and _is_domain returns True for any ACE ('xx--') label in host or tld before the _SENTENCE_WORDS/CJK exceptions. This fixes has_link_or_contact, verify, extractive, mask_links and build_surface. R4-02: gap_ok allows determiners, or one determiner plus at most 2 words from the fixed allow-list _PLAIN_MODIFIERS (long lengthy public formal official detailed). Any other skipped word fails closed, so the result no longer depends on states_quantity. _QUANTITY gained \w+ennial(ly), unanimous(ly), unanimity, fraction(s), trio(s), quartet(s), midnight, noon, gross as a second check only. Chose the allow-list over determiners-only because 3 existing tests (test_w1_d7_verbatim_numbers::test_claim_without_quantity_is_still_checked_not_quoted, test_w1_r2...::test_r2_02_excerpts_and_modifier_drops_are_still_the_brains_words, test_w1_r3...::test_r3_02_noun_phrase_modifiers_may_still_be_left_out) require 'after a long public consultation' to stay unquoted, and tests must not be weakened. Determiners-only needs owner approval to invert them. tests/web plus tests/assist: 2897 passed. New file on clean 462be42: 39 failed, 4 passed; the passes are the ordinary-text guard and the www2.refunds.xn--80asehdb case, which _OTHER's www rule already caught. The claim that real TLDs are letters-only or ACE-form comes from the RFCs; the IANA root zone list was not fetched. No graphify write commands run.

findings.evidence: _BARE requires the TLD group to be [^\W\d_]{2,24} followed by (?![\w-]), so a TLD with digits/hyphens never matches; there is no xn-- handling anywhere in uri_web or tests/web. Probe: U.has_link_or_contact('Claim at refunds.xn--p1ai now') -> False (also 'Refunds-Portal.XN--P1AI', 'refunds-portal.xn--90ais', 'bank.xn--vermgensberatung-pwb'). SY.verify('Claim your energy rebate refund at refundsportal.xn--p1ai before the deadline [1].', [src]) keeps the claim; SY.extractive('energy rebate refund deadline', [src]) picks it; build_surface(...) passes require_valid and the dumped messages contain 'refundsportal.xn--p1ai'. xn--p1ai is the ASCII (punycode) form of the delegated ccTLD .рф, which browsers resolve. The implementer's comment says the detector now fails closed for ANY label<dot>label.
findings.suggested_fix: Let the top-level label be (?:xn--[a-z0-9-]{1,59}|[^\W\d_]{2,63}) case-insensitively (or, failing closed, any [^\W_][\w-]* label containing a letter), and treat any label starting with xn-- as a link. Add a self-contained regression test parametrised over 'refundsportal.xn--p1ai', 'Refunds-Portal.XN--P1AI' and 'bank.xn--vermgensberatung-pwb' through has_link_or_contact, verify, extractive and build_surface.
findings.title: R3-01 repair still incomplete: punycode (xn--) top-level domains are not links, so they pass has_link_or_contact, verify(), the extractive path and the research surface (W1-AC15/AC12)

findings.evidence: gap_ok allows skipping one determiner plus up to MAX_GAP_WORDS=2 non-function words, and those words can be adverbs or qualifiers. states_quantity misses decennial, centennial, septennial, quinquennial, unanimous, fraction, trio, midnight, noon, gross. Probes: verify('The national census is held on decennial cycle [1].', ['The national census is held on a roughly decennial cycle.']) -> claim kept with quoted=False; the same happens for 'a near unanimous decision' -> 'unanimous decision' and 'a roughly quinquennial schedule' -> 'quinquennial schedule'. So the docstring's claim that the check 'no longer depends on recognising the quantity word' does not hold.
findings.suggested_fix: Allow a gap to drop determiners only (no modifiers), or allow only modifiers that are on a short closed list of non-qualifying adjectives; anything else quotes the source sentence. Regression test: the three source/claim pairs above must come out quoted=True or be dropped.
findings.title: R3-02 repair incomplete: _excerpt still lets a claim drop 'a <qualifier>' before an undetected quantity word (decennial, unanimous, quinquennial), so a changed quantity is shown unquoted in the Brain's words (D7)

findings.evidence: has_link_or_contact('go 退款。游戏 now') -> False; verify() keeps it, extractive() picks it and the surface shows it. 游戏 is a delegated IDN TLD and browsers map U+3002 to '.'. The implementer documents this limitation in a code comment.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend _IDN_TLDS from the IANA root zone list, or treat a short CJK run directly after U+3002 with no following CJK sentence text as a possible link.
findings.title: A Chinese/Japanese host, then U+3002, then an IDN TLD not in _IDN_TLDS is not detected as a link (documented trade-off)

findings.evidence: _BARE needs a non-[\w-] character on both sides of the domain ('(?<![\w-])' before it, '(?![\w-])' after the top-level label), and '_' is \w; the first host label also cannot start with '_'. Probe /tmp/uri_review_R5/p1.py: has_link_or_contact returns False and mask_links leaves the text unchanged for 'Claim at _refunds-portal.com_ today.', 'refunds-portal.com_', '_refunds-portal.com', '-refunds-portal.com', '__refunds.cash__', 'refunds.com-'. Probe p2.py with source 'Claim your energy rebate refund at _refunds-portal.com_ before the deadline.': verify() keeps the Brain sentence, extractive() picks it, build_surface shows the domain and require_valid accepts the surface. The same happens for '_refundsportal.xn--p1ai_'. Markdown italics/emphasis is a realistic form in retrieved web text.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not treat '_' or a trailing/leading '-' as part of the word around the domain: drop '_' and '-' from the boundary lookarounds (e.g. use (?<![^\W_]) and (?![^\W_])), or strip '_'/'-' runs at token edges before matching, and also check every token after removing edge punctuation and underscores. Add regression cases for _x.com_, x.com_, -x.com, __x.cash__ in has_link_or_contact, verify, extractive and the surface.
findings.title: R1-01 class still open: a link next to an underscore or hyphen ('_refunds-portal.com_', 'refunds-portal.com_', '-refunds-portal.com') passes has_link_or_contact, mask_links, verify(), extractive(), the research surface and the A2UI validator

findings.evidence: match(0,-1) checks gaps only when prev >= 0, so the words before the first matched word are never checked and a claim can be any trailing run of the source sentence. Probe /tmp/uri_review_R5/p4.py: verify('A plurality of voters backed the measure [1].', ['Less than a plurality of voters backed the measure.']) keeps the claim with quoted=False; the same for 'A quorum of members attended the vote' from 'Well short of a quorum of members attended the vote.' and (p3.py) 'A quintet of firms control the national market' from 'Fewer than a quintet of firms control the national market.'. states_quantity is False for these claims, so nothing else forces a quote.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the same fail-closed rule to the words left out at both ends: the claim must start at the start of the source sentence or of a clause (after a clause mark or clause word), and end at its end or at a clause boundary, with only determiners or _PLAIN_MODIFIERS dropped at the edges; otherwise quote the source sentence. Add regression cases with leading and trailing qualifiers around unlisted quantity words.
findings.title: D7 bypass at the sentence edge: _excerpt lets a claim drop a leading qualifier ('Less than', 'Fewer than', 'Well short of') before an undetected quantity word (plurality, quintet, quorum), so a changed quantity is shown unquoted in the Brain's words
